checks: Source §§1–5 gives the same facet-parallel middle anchor and at most one strictly isolated endpoint circuit. The draft correctly stipulates the affine stress and does not use existence of such a stress at other bodies or orientations.

The moving fixed-cap pullback has determinant term τ_i² δA and chord coarea 2Aτ_i, with mean opposite barycentrics τ_i/2. Comparing affine vertex motions uses n=−u_3/||u_3|| and A||u_3||=ℓ/2, giving positive coefficient 2σκ_k u_3. The dilation about the cap anchor gives T=σα_3 with that same sign.

The third-vertex equation forces w_1=w_2. Comparing the independent coefficients at vertices 1 and 2 gives κ_1=κ_2=1/2 since σ>0, w−w_3=σ, and α_1=α_2. Substitution gives 2wp²=w_3(1−2p)(1−p) and w(1+2p)+2w_3(1−p)=1, with the stated positive solution and p<1/3.

Moving the supported edge only at outward unit speed gives the middle contribution −2η and the endpoint contributions +η to the right-hand stress. The centroid chord/opposite edge ratio is 2/3, and the positive balance coefficients and coareas have the same scaling, so equal endpoint multipliers give own weighted trace (4/9)L_eℓ_e.

Both endpoint support edges are in the same outward normal direction as the middle edge; their equally parameterized midpoints give the uniform average interval containing the forced midpoint m. For caps 1 and 2 the cutting lines are transverse to all three edges, so the physical midpoint indicator inequality holds with ordinary traces almost everywhere. Cap 3 has zero middle contribution, and all its effective endpoint traces are nonnegative.

The piecewise prefix integrals about s=1/2 are nonnegative, giving an average at least 1+σ on the actual midpoint interval. AM–HM and ℓ_e+ℓ_f≤2ℓ give η(1/ℓ_e+1/ℓ_f)≥σ. Direct rational expansion yields (1−3p)(17−21p)/(9(1−p)^2)>0, so the displayed strict bound and β>2/9 under multiplier normalization follow.

overlap.comparison: Proves the non-strict 2/9 depth existence bound for all actual three planar fibers. It does not classify this restricted affine stress or give the strict endpoint compensation budget and p-dependent multipliers.
Provides an abstract labeled stress for compatible first jets in regular cases. It does not solve the assumed one-facet stress or pay its endpoint-cap term.

readability: The nonparallel cutting-line argument uses that the cap 1 and 2 normals are not collinear with the outward normal of the stressed edge; equivalently the edge is not parallel to either cutting line.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The affine stress equations force the symmetric middle profile. On the stated pair of endpoint support edges the actual weighted cap traces and reciprocal lengths give the strict normalized budget.
